skill.name: performance-gate
skill.description: Use a focused performance gate to review code for scalability, query efficiency, frontend rendering, and obvious runtime anti-patterns.
skill.summary: Review code changes for practical performance risks before release.

content.value_statement: Performance risks often appear after code works but before scale exposes weak paths. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused performance review questions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews code changes for obvious scalability, query, rendering, API, and memory risks.
Checks for N+1 queries, missing pagination, oversized payloads, and inefficient data access.
Flags frontend render patterns such as repeated sorting, inline callbacks, and missing memoization.
Provides pass or warning style review output for performance gate decisions.
Supplies Socratic questions that help teams reason about scale without over-optimizing.
limitations: Does not run benchmarks, profilers, load tests, or database explain plans.
Cannot prove performance safety without the project code and runtime context.
Focuses on obvious anti-patterns, not low-level micro-optimizations.
May need human judgment for prototypes, rare admin tasks, and small datasets.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge performance review
use_cases.description: Review a pull request for query count, pagination, rendering, and memory risks before approval.

use_cases.title: Frontend render audit
use_cases.description: Check React components for repeated calculations, unstable callbacks, large lists, and cleanup problems.

use_cases.title: Architecture readiness check
use_cases.description: Ask scale-focused questions before a new feature handles larger datasets or higher request volume.

prompt_templates.title: Basic performance gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the performance gate on my recent change. Check for obvious scalability, query, rendering, API, and memory risks. Return PASS or WARNING with concise reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Pull request warning review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request with the performance gate. Identify any N+1 queries, missing pagination, redundant API calls, expensive render work, or cleanup issues.

prompt_templates.title: Scale scenario analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this feature as if it must handle 10,000 records and then 1,000,000 records. Ask the key performance questions and list any warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-layer performance audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across backend and frontend
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the performance gate across database access, API payloads, frontend rendering, and memory lifecycle. Separate confirmed risks from context-dependent concerns.

output_examples.input: Review a list endpoint that returns all users with all fields.
output_examples.output: WARNING: Missing pagination and oversized payload risk. Ask what happens with 100,000 users and whether every returned field is needed.

output_examples.input: Review a component that sorts a large list during every render.
output_examples.output: WARNING: Expensive render work may repeat unnecessarily. Suggest memoizing the sorted result and confirming whether list virtualization is needed.

output_examples.input: Review a small admin-only report that runs once per month.
output_examples.output: PASS with note: Slow execution may be acceptable for a rare admin task. Confirm that input size remains bounded.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code path, expected data size, and usage frequency before running the gate.
Treat warnings as review prompts and confirm impact with measurements when risk is material.
Prioritize algorithmic, query, and payload fixes before minor syntax-level optimizations.
anti_patterns: Using the gate as a replacement for profiling, load testing, or production monitoring.
Optimizing prototype code without evidence that data size or traffic will grow.
Ignoring warnings about unbounded queries, repeated renders, or missing cleanup because current data is small.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews code for obvious performance risks in data access, API behavior, frontend rendering, and memory lifecycle.

faq.question: Does it run performance tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured review checklist and warning format, but it does not execute benchmarks or profilers.

faq.question: Can it help with database performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for N+1 queries, missing indexes, excessive selected columns, and missing pagination.

faq.question: Can it review frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for expensive render calculations, unstable callbacks, large lists, lazy loading opportunities, and missing cleanup.

faq.question: When should a warning block a release?
faq.answer: A warning should block release when expected data size, traffic, or user impact makes the risk likely and costly.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
